title: The Fuel Shortage Moved East, It Did Not End
subtitle: Moscow and Saint Petersburg improved, while cities, hospitals, emergency services, and filling stations elsewhere still faced severe supply failures.

source.name: Regional fuel availability reports summarized in the weekly source text

data.label: Moscow and Saint Petersburg
data.detail: Availability improved during the week, though the wider national shortage continued.

data.label: Novosibirsk
data.detail: Russia's third-largest city remained in a severe shortage.

data.label: Kursk region
data.detail: More than one third of filling stations were reported closed.

data.label: Tyumen
data.detail: Special refuelling schedules were introduced for emergency vehicles, followed by further refinery disruption.

data.label: Krasnoyarsk
data.detail: Local fuel companies failed to supply firefighters and faced a formal case.

data.label: Vladimir region
data.detail: Five hospitals, including the main emergency unit, could not find sellers for fuel tenders.

data.label: Mari El capital
data.detail: Volunteers were stationed at filling stations to manage queues and maintain order.

data.label: Irkutsk
data.detail: Supply and prices improved temporarily around a presidential visit.

data.label: Pskov
data.detail: No meaningful improvement in fuel availability was reported.

metadata.keyFinding: Improvement in the two largest cities concealed severe regional shortages elsewhere.
